samples.evidence: `seg()` is documented as covering "every interpolated identifier" (http-client.ts:21-32), but `HttpClient.base` (line 98) builds `${server}/api/v1/workspaces/${this.config.workspace}` unencoded, and the API-key routes repeat it at lines 397, 404 and 415 (`${server}/workspaces/${this.config.workspace}/api-keys`). `dry-run.ts:30` and the new `api-keys.ts:16` mirror the same raw interpolation. `workspace` is untrusted-ish input on exactly the same footing as the ids that were fixed: it comes from `--workspace` argv, `WAFFLEBASE_WORKSPACE` env, the YAML profile, or `session.activeWorkspace` (resolveConfig, config.ts:96-99/121-126/142-147). Attack: a caller/agent/CI environment that controls `WAFFLEBASE_WORKSPACE=ws-1/../../../admin` (or a poisoned `~/.wafflebase/config.yaml` profile, which is read with no validation at config.ts:169-180) makes `fetch` normalise the dot segments and send the request — with the `Authorization: Bearer <api key|JWT>` header attached by `authHeaders` (line 73-83) — to an arbitrary path on the configured server, outside the workspace prefix. That is precisely the impact the diff's own comment cites as the reason to encode ids. Note the ids can no longer be used this way (they are `%2F`-escaped), so `workspace` is now the only remaining lever.

samples.summary: Three `--dry-run` previews still print an unencoded document id, so the previewed path no longer matches the request the client would actually send.
samples.evidence: `docs/import.ts:155`, `notes/import.ts:147` and `slides/import.ts:182` print `path: \`/documents/${replace}/content\`` with `replace` raw, while the live call (`client.putDocContent(replace, doc)` → http-client.ts:300-306) now routes through `seg()`. docs/design/cli.md (added bullet) asserts "Identifiers are URL-encoded into the previewed path exactly as the client encodes them into the real request, so the printed URL is the URL that would be fetched" — false for these three `--replace` paths. Impact is a misleading preview: `wafflebase docs import x.docx --replace '../../admin' --dry-run` prints a traversal-shaped path that suggests the real request escapes the workspace prefix (it does not), and conversely a reviewer auditing previews cannot rely on them to reflect the wire request.

samples.summary: The new doc bullet states as a blanket contract that "A dry run never reaches the network", but `login` ignores `--dry-run`: it performs the OAuth exchange and writes credentials to disk.
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts` has no `dryRun` check anywhere in its action (lines 12-60 read the global opts only for `server`); with `--dry-run` it still starts a local callback HTTP server, opens the browser, POSTs to `${server}/auth/cli/exchange` (line 56), fetches `/auth/me` and `/workspaces`, and calls `saveSession(...)` — persisting an access and refresh token to `~/.wafflebase/session.json`. A flag documented as "prints the request that would be sent — without executing it" that instead mints and stores a live credential is a state mutation a caller was told would not happen. Either scope the doc sentence to the API namespaces or gate `login`.

verdict.reason: Verified directly in the tree. `seg()` (http-client.ts:30-32) claims to cover "every interpolated identifier" (http-client.ts:20-28), but `HttpClient.base` interpolates `this.config.workspace` unencoded (http-client.ts:98) into every `request()` URL (http-client.ts:186), which carries the `Authorization: Bearer` header (http-client.ts:73-83). The API-key routes repeat the raw interpolation (http-client.ts:397, 404, 415 — line 415 even `seg()`-encodes the key id while leaving `workspace` raw), and the previews mirror it (dry-run.ts:30, api-keys.ts:16-17). `workspace` reaches the client unvalidated from `--workspace` argv (root.ts:33, root.ts:66), `WAFFLEBASE_WORKSPACE` (config.ts:98/123/145/162), the YAML profile parsed with no validation (config.ts:169-180), or `session.activeWorkspace` (config.ts:124); a grep of packages/cli/src found no format check anywhere on that path. A value like `ws-1/../../../admin` (or one containing `?`/`#`) is normalised by the WHATWG parser inside `fetch`, sending the credentialed request to an arbitrary path outside the workspace prefix — the exact impact the change's own comment cites. In-lane (path traversal / unsafe input handling) and a real gap in the newly added guard, not a hypothetical.

finding.summary: `--dry-run` is silently ignored by `api-keys create` / `revoke` / `list`, so the documented "preview a write first" safety control mints or destroys a real credential
finding.evidence:
This PR sweeps `--dry-run` across the remaining read commands and, at docs/design/cli.md:824-827, now states the contract unconditionally: "A dry run never reaches the network, so it burns no rate limit and emits no access log." The credential-management commands are the one namespace that was never swept. `registerApiKeysCommand` never reads `opts.dryRun`: api-keys.ts:15-17 goes straight to `getClient(opts).createApiKey(name)`, :43-45 to `revokeApiKey(keyId)`, :29-31 to `listApiKeys()`. Commander accepts the global `--dry-run` on every subcommand (root.ts:75), so the flag parses and is discarded.

Attack/failure chain: the CLI is explicitly aimed at agents, and the agent guidance says to preview writes with the flag — packages/cli/skills/SKILL.md:67 ("For write operations, run with `--dry-run` first to show intent"), docs/design/cli.md:905 ("`write` … Agent should confirm or use `--dry-run` first") and :1027. `wafflebase api-keys create ci-key --dry-run` therefore issues a live POST that mints a workspace-scoped API key and prints its secret (`schema/registry.ts:579` declares the response as `{ id, name, prefix, key }`) to stdout — into whatever agent transcript/CI log the user believed was showing an inert preview, with no revocation ever performed. `wafflebase api-keys revoke <id> --dry-run` (registry.ts:593 marks it `destructive`) irreversibly revokes the key the user was only asking to preview, breaking every consumer of that key. Both are credential-lifecycle side effects taken under a flag whose whole contract is "no side effect".

Every other write/destructive path in the CLI honours the flag (cells.ts:62/95/143, tabs.ts:47/71, docs.ts:108/143/161, files.ts:118/136, docs|notes|slides import), which is what makes the gap read as covered.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts `registerApiKeysCommand` never reads `opts.dryRun` and goes straight to the network. The actual file does the opposite: all three subcommands short-circuit on `opts.dryRun` before any client call. `create` prints `printDryRunUrl(apiKeysUrl(opts), 'POST', { name })` and returns at api-keys.ts:34-37, ahead of `createApiKey(name)` at :38; `list` returns at :52-55 ahead of `listApiKeys()` at :56; `revoke` returns at :72-75 ahead of `revokeApiKey(keyId)` at :76. `printDryRunUrl` (client/dry-run.ts:41-52) only console.logs a JSON preview and issues no request, so no key is minted, no secret is printed, and no revocation occurs. A dedicated `apiKeysUrl` helper (api-keys.ts:13-18) was added specifically because these routes are not under the v1 base, showing the namespace was deliberately swept. Tests cover all three cases at test/read-dry-run.test.ts:230-260. A repo-wide grep for `dryRun` lists packages/cli/src/commands/api-keys.ts among matches, contradicting the reviewer's stated search result.

mergedFrom.summary: Document/tab/cell identifiers are interpolated into request paths unencoded, so a crafted identifier redirects the authenticated request to an arbitrary path on the configured server (mirrored verbatim by the new dry-run preview)

finding.summary: Document/tab/cell identifiers are interpolated into request paths without encodeURIComponent, so a caller-supplied id can retarget the credentialed request outside the workspace scope (path traversal / request-target injection)
finding.evidence: `getDocument(id)` builds `GET ${base}/documents/${id}` with no encoding (http-client.ts:199); same pattern at :330 listTabs, :340/:342 getCells (docId/tabId raw, only `range` encoded), :345 getCell, :348 setCell, :354 deleteCell, :361 batchCells. `base` is `${server}/api/v1/workspaces/${workspace}` (:82-85). `fetch` parses the string with the WHATWG URL parser, which collapses dot segments, so `docId = "../../../../workspaces/victim-ws/api-keys"` turns `wafflebase docs get <id>` into `GET ${server}/workspaces/victim-ws/api-keys` with the user's `Authorization: Bearer ...` header attached — i.e. the client-side workspace scoping in the path is bypassable and any endpoint on the configured host can be reached with the caller's credentials (only server-side authz stands between). The boundary is real because the CLI is explicitly built to be driven by agents (docs/design/cli.md:22-26, 1024-1029), which routinely pass document ids taken from untrusted content; the CLI then acts as a confused deputy. `downloadFileDocument` already uses `encodeURIComponent(docId)` (:254), showing the intended convention the other builders skip. The change under review propagates the same unencoded interpolation into new code (cells.ts:24, docs.ts:126, tabs.ts:15). Confidence is medium because exploitability depends on the backend's own authorization on the reached endpoint and on ids coming from an untrusted source.

verdict.reason: The described unencoded path interpolation does not exist in this repository. `packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:20-32` defines `seg(value) = encodeURIComponent(value)` specifically to prevent the described dot-segment/`?` retargeting, and every identifier the finding names is passed through it: getDocument/updateDocument/deleteDocument (:213,:216,:219), listTabs/createTab/renameTab (:344,:347,:350 — docId and tabId), getCells/getCell/setCell/deleteCell/batchCells (:360,:366,:372,:379,:389 — docId, tabId and sref, not merely `range`), the content endpoints (:297,:303,:314,:320,:331,:337), downloadFileDocument (:268) and revokeApiKey (:415). The cited line numbers do not match: :199 is `return { ok: res.ok, status: res.status, data };`. The claimed propagation sites are encoded as well — cells.ts:24, tabs.ts:15, docs.ts:126 all use `seg()` imported from client/dry-run.ts:12-14 (also encodeURIComponent). An exhaustive grep for `/documents/${`, `/tabs/${`, `/cells/${`, `/files/${`, `api-keys/${` across packages/cli/src yields only three unencoded occurrences (docs/import.ts:155, notes/import.ts:147, slides/import.ts:182), and all three are inside `if (dryRun)` branches that only JSON.stringify a preview to stdout; the corresponding live call (docs/import.ts:162 `client.putDocContent(replace, doc)`) encodes via http-client.ts:300-306. No credentialed request can be retargeted off the workspace prefix by a caller-supplied id.
